I need you to help me produce a complete revised research proposal JSON. I'll give you the context and the specific changes needed. Please output ONLY the complete JSON object.

## Context
This is round 5 revision of a research proposal about TSA-GRPO (Tokenization-Structure-Aware GRPO), which augments GRPO with tokenization-aware process rewards for character-level and code-level reasoning.

## Three Issues to Fix

### Issue 1 (MODERATE): Cherry-picked variable renaming evidence
The proposal cited "Gemini-3 showing a 31.9pp drop from variable renaming" from arXiv 2505.10443. But the paper's ACTUAL findings show:
- Variable renaming: 8/9 models IMPROVED (+1.5 to +14.4pp). The paper states "variable renaming consistently improves accuracy for most open-access models." Only Gemini-3 dropped (-31.9pp).
- Loop unrolling: ALL 9 models dropped catastrophically (-22.3 to -70.4pp)
- If-else swap: ALL models dropped (-4.8 to -28.6pp)  
- Loop conversion: ALL models dropped (-4.2 to -44.7pp)
- Expression mirroring: 8/9 dropped (-1.5 to -24pp)
- Also: models produce correct predictions from flawed reasoning 10-50% of the time

FIX NEEDED: Replace ALL cherry-picked Gemini-3 citations with honest characterization. Use structural mutation evidence (especially loop unrolling) as the universally harmful evidence. This STRENGTHENS the motivation.

### Issue 2 (MINOR): Downstream code evaluation focus  
Since variable renaming doesn't consistently degrade modern LLMs, "ReCode-Rename" evaluation may show weak baselines.

FIX NEEDED: Replace "ReCode-Rename" with "ReCode-Mutate" - evaluate on the FULL ReCode perturbation suite (docstring, naming, syntax, format). Set differential expectations:
- Naming perturbations: baseline drops may be minimal; measure output consistency/sensitivity rather than just accuracy drop
- Syntax perturbations (dead code insertion): moderate expected improvement
- Structural perturbations: exploratory, tests broader robustness transfer
Keep word recovery probes. Also add a brief practical significance anchor: TokDrift shows up to 60% output change rates; 2505.10443 shows 10-50% correct-but-flawed-reasoning rate.

### Issue 3 (MINOR): NAACL 2027 venue pathway
ARR October 2026 cycle exists but has NO confirmed commitment venues. NAACL 2027 is not listed on the ARR dates page.

FIX NEEDED: Flag as "unconfirmed/speculative" explicitly.

## Complete JSON to revise
Here is the original proposal. Make ALL changes described above throughout EVERY relevant field (core_problem, opportunity, landscape, downstream_transfer_evaluation, description, target_venues, reviewer_response, change_summary). Be thorough - the variable renaming correction touches many fields.

IMPORTANT RULES:
1. Output change_type: "minor"
2. Keep ALL existing content that doesn't need changing
3. Be honest and precise about the 2505.10443 findings everywhere they're cited
4. The structural mutation evidence actually STRENGTHENS the code robustness motivation (universal, not model-specific)
5. Keep CodeIdBench and TokDrift motivation intact (those are about tokenization sensitivity, still valid)
6. Add practical significance: "2505.10443 found code LLMs produce correct predictions from flawed reasoning in 10-50% of cases, and TokDrift shows up to 60% output change rates from single naming convention rewrites—establishing that tokenization-induced code fragility is a practical concern affecting real-world deployment reliability"

Here are the SPECIFIC text replacements needed:

### In core_problem:
Replace: "recent evaluation on modern LLMs including Qwen2.5-Coder and Gemini-3 confirms persistent sensitivity, with Gemini-3 showing a 31.9pp drop from variable renaming alone, per arXiv 2505.10443"
With: "recent evaluation on modern LLMs (arXiv 2505.10443) confirms persistent and universal sensitivity to structural mutations: loop unrolling causes -22pp to -70pp drops across all 9 tested models (including Qwen2.5-Coder at -44.3pp and GPT-5.2 at -68.1pp), if-else swap causes -5pp to -29pp drops, and loop conversion causes -4pp to -45pp drops; notably, while variable renaming improved accuracy for 8/9 models, the paper found models produce correct predictions from flawed reasoning in 10-50% of cases"

### In core_problem also:
Replace: "identifier renaming causes significant performance drops in code generation (ReCode documented 56-82% worst-case drops on 2023 models; recent evaluation on modern LLMs including Qwen2.5-Coder and Gemini-3 confirms persistent sensitivity, with Gemini-3 showing a 31.9pp drop from variable renaming alone, per arXiv 2505.10443)"
With: "semantics-preserving code mutations cause severe performance degradation: ReCode (ACL 2023) documented 56-82% worst-case drops on 2023 models, and recent evaluation on 9 modern LLMs including Qwen2.5-Coder, GPT-5.2, and Gemini-3 (arXiv 2505.10443) confirms universal vulnerability—loop unrolling alone causes -22pp to -70pp drops across ALL tested models, while even for variable renaming (which improved accuracy for 8/9 models), the study found models produce correct predictions based on flawed reasoning 10-50% of the time"

### In opportunity:
Replace all references to "Gemini-3 showing a 31.9pp drop from variable renaming" with the corrected structural mutation evidence.

### In landscape:
Replace the parenthetical about 2505.10443 with honest characterization:
Old: "recent evaluation by arXiv 2505.10443 on modern LLMs including Qwen2.5-Coder, Qwen3-Coder, and Gemini-3 confirms persistent sensitivity, with Gemini-3 showing a 31.9pp drop from variable renaming and loop unrolling causing 35-44pp drops"
New: "recent evaluation by arXiv 2505.10443 on 9 modern LLMs confirms that while variable renaming improved accuracy for 8/9 models, structural mutations universally degrade performance—loop unrolling causes -22pp to -70pp drops across all models, if-else swap causes -5pp to -29pp drops—and models produce correct predictions from flawed reasoning 10-50% of the time"

### In downstream_transfer_evaluation:
Replace "ReCode-Rename" section entirely with "ReCode-Mutate" approach:
- Evaluate on FULL ReCode perturbation suite (all 4 categories)
- Acknowledge honest variable renaming findings
- Set differential expectations per mutation type
- Primary metric: per-mutation-type robustness analysis rather than single "Robust Drop" number
- Expected outcome: ≥15% relative reduction in Robust Drop on SYNTAX and STRUCTURAL perturbations (not renaming-specific)
- Add word recovery probes comparing models under different mutation types
- Add practical significance paragraph

### In description:
Fix all corresponding references to match the corrected evidence.
Replace "ReCode-Rename" references with "ReCode-Mutate" and update the evaluation description.
Replace "Gemini-3 drops 31.9pp from variable renaming" with "loop unrolling causes -22pp to -70pp drops across all 9 models"

### In target_venues:
For the NAACL 2027 entry, add explicit "(UNCONFIRMED — no commitment venues listed for October 2026 ARR cycle as of May 2026)"

### In reviewer_response:
Add round 5 responses for all 3 issues.

### change_summary:
Describe all changes made in this round.

Now please write the COMPLETE JSON object with all fields. Include change_type: "minor" as a new field. Every field from the original must be present (possibly modified). The JSON should be valid and complete.

Original fields to include (keep unchanged unless specified above):
- title (unchanged)
- project_name (unchanged)  
- source (unchanged)
- level (unchanged - "strong-minus")
- key_references (add "Are Large Language Models Robust in Understanding Code Against Semantics-Preserving Mutations? (arXiv:2505.10443)" if not already present - it IS present, keep it)
- approach (unchanged except any references to Gemini-3 variable renaming)
- code_identifier_evaluation (unchanged)
- generalization_beyond_primary_domains (unchanged)
- resource_estimate (update if needed - add note about broader ReCode eval)
- inspired_by (update if needed)

Please produce the complete JSON. Make sure it's valid JSON (proper escaping of quotes, etc.).

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
